steps: Anchor: the GST Council was created by the 101st Amendment under Article 279A, not 269A, so I is incorrect; strike (b) and (d), which lack I.
Left with (a) I and IV vs (c) I and III. Test IV: decisions need three-fourths of weighted votes - that is the real rule, so IV is correct; strike (a).
Check III: every State has an equal vote (States share 2/3 weight equally), so III is incorrect as written.
-> answer (c) I and III

underline.text: Every state does not have an equal vote

fact: The GST Council is set up under Article 279A; decisions need a 3/4 weighted majority and each State has an equal vote.

steps: A 'severe crisis' must be described by bad indicators only.
(b) and (c) list only good signs (surplus, high reserves) - strike; (d) mixes 'strong inflows, low inflation' - strike.
-> answer (a) high inflation, low forex reserves and large fiscal deficit
fact: In 1991 India had double-digit inflation, forex reserves for about two weeks of imports and a fiscal deficit near 8% of GDP.

steps: Purvodaya means 'rise of the east' - IV (primary goal is Gujarat) is absurd; strike (c) and (d), which contain IV.
Left (a) I, II vs (b) I, II, III. Test III: the Budget 2024 corridor was Amritsar-Kolkata, not New Delhi-Kolkata, so III is false; strike (b).
-> answer (a) I, II only
fact: Purvodaya (Budget July 2024) targets the eastern States; its corridor is Amritsar-Kolkata and it includes the Buxar-Bhagalpur expressway.

steps: III says modern farming is 'unrelated' to freshwater depletion - an absolute denial, and false (irrigation is the biggest water user); strike (b) and (c).
IV says monoculture 'supports ecosystem stability' - false, monoculture cuts biodiversity; strike (a).
-> answer (d) I and II
fact: Agrochemicals pollute soil and water and monocultures reduce ecosystem stability; sustainable farming protects soil and biodiversity.

steps: India always runs a merchandise trade deficit, so (a) merchandise exports cannot be the reason; strike.
India's strong side in the current account is net services (IT, business services) - RBI credited the Q4 2023-24 surplus to services exports.
-> answer (b) surge in services exports
fact: India's current account surplus of 0.6% of GDP in Q4 2023-24 came mainly from strong net services exports.

steps: The 1991 reforms were Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation (LPG).
(a), (b), (d) are the opposite of LPG (more control, less trade, weaker private sector); strike them.
-> answer (c) enhanced global integration
fact: The 1991 LPG reforms integrated India with the global economy through trade and foreign investment.

steps: Anchor IV: in November 2024 RBI issued a framework to reclassify FPI holdings above 10% as FDI - true; strike (a), which lacks IV, and (d).
Anchor I: the rupee stayed relatively stable despite FPI outflows (RBI intervention) - true; strike (b), which lacks I.
-> answer (c) all the above
fact: In 2024-25 RBI issued a framework to reclassify FPI investment beyond the 10% limit as FDI, while the rupee stayed stable.

steps: National income has exactly three standard methods: product (value added), income and expenditure.
(a), (b), (c) are those three; 'cost and accounting' is a business-accounting term, the odd one.
-> answer (d) cost and accounting method
fact: National income is measured by the value added (product), income and expenditure methods.

steps: Anchor II: the 1956 Resolution (Mahalanobis era) put 17 industries in Schedule A for the public sector - true; strike (c).
III: it stressed cottage and small industries - true; strike (a). I: licensing under IDRA 1951 continued - true; strike (b).
-> answer (d) I, II, III
fact: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 gave the public sector the lead (three schedules), kept licensing and stressed small industries.

steps: Investment that responds to a change in income is 'induced' (accelerator); investment independent of income is 'autonomous'.
Gross/net investment are about depreciation, not income; strike (a), (b), and (d) is the opposite concept.
-> answer (c) induced investment

underline.text: due to change in the level of national income

fact: Induced investment changes with the level of income; autonomous investment does not.

steps: (a), (c), (d) are textbook definitions and are true.
Direct quote = units of HOME currency per one unit of foreign currency (Rs 84 = $1); (b) reverses it, which is the indirect quote.
-> answer (b)

underline.text: number of units of a foreign currency exchangeable for one unit of home currency

fact: A direct quote gives home currency per unit of foreign currency; the reverse is the indirect quote.

steps: Recall Budget 2025-26: fiscal deficit RE 2024-25 = 4.8% of GDP, so A is true.
The FRBM glide path promised below 4.5% for 2025-26; BE was 4.4%, lower than 4.8%, so B is true.
-> answer (c) both statements are correct
fact: Union Budget 2025-26: fiscal deficit 4.8% of GDP (RE 2024-25) and 4.4% (BE 2025-26).

steps: Check the body: Labour Bureau is a separate body (strike c); the Economic Survey is the Finance Ministry's (strike b).
NSO launched the Periodic Labour Force Survey in 2017 to replace the old quinquennial rounds; QES covers establishments, not unemployment.
-> answer (d) Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)
fact: Since 2017 the NSO measures unemployment through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).

steps: Farm work peaks at sowing and harvest and is idle in between - unemployment that comes with seasons.
Cyclical = business cycle, structural = skill/capital mismatch, frictional = between jobs; strike.
-> answer (b) seasonal unemployment
fact: Seasonal unemployment is the type most linked with agriculture.

steps: 'Deposit facility' means banks park money with RBI, i.e. RBI absorbs liquidity; strike (a) and (d), which inject liquidity.
Its novelty over reverse repo is that RBI need not give G-secs as collateral; (c) is not its purpose.
-> answer (b) absorbing surplus liquidity without collateral
fact: The SDF (2022), the floor of the LAF corridor, lets RBI absorb surplus liquidity without collateral.

steps: IV (increase operational expenses) cannot be a regulator's goal; strike (d).
I, II and III are the standard benefits of faster settlement (liquidity, less counterparty risk, less volatility exposure), so keep all three.
-> answer (c) I, II, III only
fact: SEBI's T+0 settlement aims to raise liquidity and cut settlement and counterparty risk.

steps: Check the body: fiscal policy (tax and spending) belongs to the Government, not RBI.
Forex reserves, market intervention and the market-based LERMS framework are RBI tools; keep them out.
-> answer (a) fiscal policy adjustments
fact: RBI manages exchange-rate volatility with forex reserves and market intervention; fiscal policy is the Government's.

steps: The rupee trade settlement mechanism (Special Rupee Vostro Accounts) exists to internationalise the rupee.
(a) is the opposite; (c) 'eliminates' reserves is extreme; (d) higher costs cannot be a policy aim; strike.
-> answer (b) encourages use of the Indian currency in cross-border trade

underline.text: encourage the use of the Indian currency

fact: RBI's rupee invoicing and settlement mechanism under FTP 2023 promotes the rupee in cross-border trade.

steps: Articles 292-293 sit together: 292 = borrowing by the Union, 293 = borrowing by States.
Article 293(2) lets the Government of India lend to States; 294-295 are about succession to property and liabilities.
-> answer (b) Article 293
fact: Article 293(2) empowers the Centre to give loans to States; Article 292 covers Union borrowing.

steps: Recall: India ranked 38th of 139 in LPI 2023, up from 44th in 2018.
Without recall, the middle values 27 and 38 are the likely pair; 15 is too high for India, 49 below its 2018 rank.
-> answer (c) 38
fact: India ranked 38th of 139 countries in the World Bank Logistics Performance Index 2023.

steps: A deflator is a price index; a rise means the general price level went up.
Higher prices mean each rupee buys less; strike (a), (c) and (d).
-> answer (b) decreases purchasing power
fact: A rising GNP deflator means higher prices, so the purchasing power of money falls.

steps: Check the body: a scheme for livestock comes from the line department for livestock.
The Credit Guarantee Scheme (2024) sits under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund of DAHD; Finance Ministry, NABARD and RBI are distractors.
-> answer (d) Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying

underline.text: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying

fact: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying launched the Credit Guarantee Scheme for the livestock sector (2024).

steps: Buying low in one market and selling high in another at the same time is the textbook definition of arbitrage.
Annuity is a series of payments, 'rationalization' is unrelated and 'Semi Bombla' is a made-up word; strike.
-> answer (a) arbitrage
fact: Arbitrage is buying where the price is lower and selling at the same time where it is higher.

steps: SDRs are 'paper gold': an IMF reserve asset with no notes, coins or metal behind them.
Strike (a), (b), (c), which give a physical form; here the 'only' option is the true one.
-> answer (d) book keeping entry only
fact: SDRs exist only as book entries in IMF accounts and are called paper gold.

steps: Anchor: foreign currency assets are the largest part of India's reserves; strike (b), which lacks them.
RBI's weekly data list four parts: FCA, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position in the IMF; strike (a) and (c).
-> answer (d) all the above
fact: India's forex reserves are foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position with the IMF.

steps: Stagflation = inflation + stagnation; anything raising prices or cutting output 'could potentially' add to it.
a (inflationary spending), b (falling output), c (weak demand) and d (weaker exports) each push one side; the soft wording 'could potentially' allows all.
-> answer (d) all the above
fact: Stagflation is high inflation together with stagnant output and growth.

steps: c says FDI rose 'without decreasing in any Financial Year' after the sector was 'entirely' reformed - stacked extremes, false; strike (a) and (c).
b (increased) and d (decreased) contradict each other, so (b), which has both, is struck.
Survey 2023 said FDI fell in 2022 because of the weak global situation, in line with the global trend.
-> answer (d) d only

underline.text: without decreasing in any Financial Year

fact: Economic Survey 2022-23: FDI inflows fell in 2022 because of the weak global economic situation.

steps: India has run a trade deficit every year since liberalisation, so imports have grown more than exports.
(a), (b), (d) are the standard gains of globalisation; keep them out.
-> answer (c)

underline.text: Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports

fact: Since 1991 India's imports have grown faster than exports, giving a persistent trade deficit.

steps: Under the old classification, non-plan spending = committed items: interest, defence, subsidies, salaries.
Sectoral development spending (S&T, agriculture) was mostly plan expenditure; strike (b), (c) and (d).
-> answer (a) interest payments
fact: Interest payments were the largest item of the Centre's non-plan expenditure.

steps: AP fact: Andhra Pradesh is a Front Runner in SDG Index 2023-24 - b true; strike (c) and (d), which lack b.
Left (a) a, b vs (b) b, c. The Achiever category needs a score of 100; no State reached it, so c is false; strike (b).
-> answer (a) a, b only correct
fact: SDG India Index 2023-24: India 71, Kerala and Uttarakhand top with 79, and AP is a Front Runner.

steps: GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies.
Direct taxes are paid out of factor income and depreciation separates gross from net; strike (a), (b), (d).
-> answer (c) indirect taxes and subsidies

underline.text: GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices

fact: GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies.

steps: A: devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer, so the trade balance improves - true.
R: devaluation lowers, not raises, export prices in foreign currency - false.
-> answer (c) (A) is true and (R) is false
fact: Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports costlier, which tends to improve the trade balance.

steps: Factories Act Section 2(n): the 'occupier' is the person with ultimate control over the factory's affairs.
The manager runs it day to day; chairman and MD are company titles, not Act terms; strike.
-> answer (a) occupier
fact: Under the Factories Act 1948 the occupier is the person with ultimate control over the factory.

steps: 'Justify the entire budget from the beginning' = start every item from zero.
Functional and master budgets build on past figures; strike (a), (b), (d).
-> answer (c) zero-base budgeting

underline.text: justify his entire budget in detail from beginning

fact: Zero-base budgeting requires every budget item to be justified afresh each year.

steps: Deflator = nominal GDP / real GDP x 100, i.e. current prices over constant prices.
(b) gives the ratio upside down; (a) and (c) are meaningless; strike.
-> answer (d) GDP at current prices to constant prices
fact: The GDP deflator is GDP at current prices divided by GDP at constant prices.

steps: Devaluation, import tariffs and attracting FDI all act directly on the external accounts.
Cutting spending on domestic projects is a general fiscal step, not a standard BoP tool - the odd one.
-> answer (c)

underline.text: Reducing government spending on domestic projects

fact: Standard BoP correction tools are devaluation, import controls and attracting capital such as FDI.

steps: (b), (c), (d) all use 'only' to cut the BoP down to one part - lean false and clearly wrong.
The BoP has two main parts: current account and capital account.
-> answer (a)
fact: The balance of payments has two main parts, the current account and the capital account.

steps: A: transfer earnings (pensions, subsidies, gifts) are left out of national income - true.
R: they are not payments for factor services - true.
Does R explain A? Yes - NI counts only factor incomes, so non-factor payments are excluded.
-> answer (a)
fact: Transfer payments are excluded from national income because they are not earned by factor services.

steps: Surest pair: Fiscal Policy - Tax Rate (d-i); strike (c) and (d).
Second pair: Trade Policy - Imports and Exports (b-iii); strike (b), which has b-ii.
Check: Monetary - Bank Rate, Credit - Margin fit.
-> answer (a) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
fact: Bank rate is a monetary tool, margin requirements a credit control, tax rates a fiscal tool.

steps: Two-way trade in the same product = trade within one industry.
(a) and (b) are invented phrases; factor reversal is a Heckscher-Ohlin concept; strike.
-> answer (d) intra-industry trade

underline.text: simultaneously imports and exports the same product

fact: Intra-industry trade is a country importing and exporting the same kind of product.

steps: India imports over 85% of its crude, so its problem is dependence on world supply.
(a) no demand, (b) steady prices and (d) abundant reserves are false or not challenges; strike.
-> answer (c) supply chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices
fact: India imports more than 85% of its crude oil, which leaves it exposed to supply shocks and price swings.

steps: The 1991 policy removed controls; it did not tweak them.
(a), (b), (c) keep the convertibility clause with different scopes; only (d) removes it, which fits deregulation.
-> answer (d) the mandatory convertible clause is no longer applicable
fact: The 1991 Industrial Policy dropped the mandatory convertibility clause on term loans from financial institutions.

steps: High-powered money (M0) H = currency with public + bank cash reserves + other deposits with RBI.
Time deposits belong to broad money M3, not H; strike (d). (a) and (b) each miss one part; strike.
-> answer (c)

underline.text: Time deposits of the commercial banks
Currency held by the public + Cash reserves of the commercial banks + Other deposits with the RBI

fact: High-powered money is currency with the public plus banks' reserves plus other deposits with RBI.

steps: (b) 'removal of all' restrictions and (c) 'nationalization of all' banks are extremes that never happened; strike.
(d) expanding PSUs does not ease private business; strike.
-> answer (a) introduction of GST
fact: GST, which replaced many indirect taxes with one, is a key reform that improved Ease of Doing Business.

steps: Anchor: electricity supply has never been brought under GST; strike (a) and (c), which lack iii.
Charitable entities' specified services are GST-exempt; strike (b), which lacks iv.
Petrol/diesel are kept out for now and liquor is excluded by the Constitution, so all four.
-> answer (d) all of the above
fact: Petroleum fuels, liquor for human use, electricity and specified charitable services are outside or exempt from GST.

steps: A: Economic Survey 2023-24 reported 8.2% real GDP growth in FY24 - true.
R: the Survey credits macroeconomic stability with limiting the external shocks - true.
R explains A (it is the Survey's own reasoning).
-> answer (a)
fact: India's real GDP grew 8.2% in FY24, which the Survey credits to macroeconomic stability.

steps: The Planning Commission was abolished in 2015; strike (a).
RBI and the Finance Ministry do not prepare poverty indices; NITI Aayog publishes the National MPI with OPHI-UNDP methods.

fact: NITI Aayog prepares India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index.

steps: A: India stayed resilient amid geopolitical shocks - true (Survey theme).
R: post-COVID fiscal and monetary policies kept stability - true.
Policy-led stability is exactly why the economy was resilient, so R explains A.
-> answer (a)

underline.text: fiscal and monetary policies ensured economic and financial stability

fact: The Economic Survey links India's resilience to post-COVID fiscal and monetary policy that kept stability.

steps: 'Fine-tuning' operations go both ways: variable rate repo (inject) and reverse repo (absorb).
(a), (b), (d) each give one direction only; strike.

underline.text: in alignment with the monetary policy stance

fact: RBI's fine-tuning operations inject or absorb liquidity to keep it aligned with the policy stance.

fact: Bharat Rice was launched in February 2024 at Rs 29 per kg.
